title: Red Dragon Onion: Characteristics
metaDescription: Red Dragon onion is an onion variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Red Dragon is an onion variety. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Onion plants in beds separated by grassy paths on a Philippine farm, the kind of farm where Red Dragon onion is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [onion variety finder](/crop-varieties/onion), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for onion and garlic](/land-preparation/onion-garlic-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: 85 to 90 days after transplanting. Yield, by the seller's count: 25 to 30 t/ha potential (seller), about 25 t/ha on the Pangasinan farm. No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit onion fields most often: [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [onion armyworm](/pests/onion-armyworm), [purple blotch of onion](/diseases/purple-blotch), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 85 to 90 days after transplanting.
**Yield:** 25 to 30 t/ha potential (seller), about 25 t/ha on the Pangasinan farm.
**Fruit:** Compact, even, bright to dark red globe bulbs.
Stores very well, up to eight months in cold storage is claimed.
Stands up to bulb rot, purple blotch, leafminer, damping off, leaf twisting and lis lis (seller's claim).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a Bayambang, Pangasinan grower planted 15 ha, got about 25 t/ha and went to 50 ha the next season, featured at Ramgo's Bongabon onion festival. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual onion on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Red Dragon onion

Red onion stores longer, while yellow onion yields more. Pick a variety that bulbs in the short days of the Philippine dry season, and plant it after the rains so the bulbs dry well. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.
